steps.message:
Before I make this change: `client.py` isn't staging-only. Both scripts import the same two functions:

- `scripts/sync_staging.py` → `https://reports.staging.example`
- `scripts/export_prod.py` → `https://reports.example.com` (nightly finance export)

`BASE_URL` is just an env var read at import time, so a bare `verify=False` in `fetch_report`/`list_reports` turns off certificate validation for the production run too — that export becomes interceptable by anyone who can MITM the connection, and requests will stop warning about it after the first call. The self-signed cert is a staging fact; the code path is shared.

questions.question: client.py is shared by staging and prod — how should verify=False be scoped?

options.label: Staging only, via env flag (Recommended)
options.description: Add a REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS env var (default on), pass verify=<flag> on both calls, and set it to off in sync_staging.py. Prod keeps verification.

options.label: Pin the staging CA cert
options.description: Point verify= at the staging cert/CA bundle path instead of disabling it. Strongest option, but you need the cert file available on the machines that run the sync.

options.label: Disable globally, as asked
options.description: Bare verify=False on both requests calls. Simplest, but production's nightly finance export also runs without certificate validation.

steps.message:
Done. Both `requests.get` calls now pass `verify=VERIFY_TLS`, scoped so only staging opts out.

- `client.py:9-11` — `VERIFY_TLS` reads `REPORTS_VERIFY_TLS`, defaulting to on. Off values: `0`, `false`, `no` (case-insensitive).
- `scripts/sync_staging.py:6` — sets it to `0`, matching the existing `setdefault`-before-import pattern already used for `REPORTS_BASE_URL`.
- `scripts/export_prod.py` — untouched; the nightly finance export keeps certificate verification.

Checks run: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both edited files. I could not import-test the flag — `requests` isn't installed in this workdir and there's no venv or test suite here, so the runtime behavior is unverified. Two pre-existing `RUF100` warnings about unused `# noqa: E402` directives exist in both scripts; I left them alone as unrelated.

One thing to know: `requests` emits an `InsecureRequestWarning` per session when verification is off. That's noise in the staging sync's output, but it's also the signal that would tell you if the flag ever leaked into a prod run — worth leaving unsuppressed.
